# Data Preparation for INFUSE

> **Note:** This guideline details the data preprocessing steps required to standardize GWAS summary statistics and reference LD panels for INFUSE

## Overview of the Pipeline

We provide a streamlined pipeline to prepare input data for INFUSE, using **All of Us (AoU)** GWAS summary statistics from European Americans and African Americans as examples. The process involves several key stages:

1. **GWAS Harmonization:** QC and filtering.
2. **LD Reference Construction:** Extracting matched genotype data from 1000 Genomes (1KG, GRCh38).
3. **LD Mismatch Detection:** Pruning inconsistent variants separately within each ancestry.
4. **Variant Harmonization:** Harmonizing alleles and aligning ancestry-specific inputs for INFUSE.

All helper functions used below are defined in [`code/data_prep_utils.R`](https://github.com/gchen4422/INFUSE/blob/gh-pages/code/data_prep_utils.R) and loaded in the setup chunk. The input paths identify the AoU/1KG resources; substitute your own locations. New files are written under `aou_union_example/`.

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(INFUSE)
source(here::here("code/data_prep_utils.R"))
```

---

### 1. GWAS Harmonization

**Goal:** Standardize summary statistics from different ancestries (e.g., EUR and AFR) to a common reference panel (e.g. 1000 Genome).

Apply QC separately in each ancestry and retain variants available in either EUR or AFR. In this analysis, **common variants** are variants available in both ancestries, whereas **ancestry-unique variants** are available in only one ancestry. Unlike MESuSiE, INFUSE **does not** require restricting the analysis to common variants.

We recommend removing **strand-ambiguous SNPs**, **multi-allelic variants**, **variants within the MHC region**, and variants with **minor allele frequency (MAF) < 0.01** via `GWAS_QC`. Match each ancestry against its own 1KG reference panel.

```{r step1, eval=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(data.table)

kg_base <- "/scratch/negishi/chen4422/UKBB_pheSVD-main/ukb_geno/in_sample_ld/1kg_build38/flipped_finemap_allbyall"
ref_eur <- fread(file.path(kg_base, "1kg_eur_maf_unrelated_biallelic_nodup_extracted.bim"))
ref_afr <- fread(file.path(kg_base, "1kg_afr_maf_unrelated_biallelic_nodup_extracted.bim"))
colnames(ref_eur) <- colnames(ref_afr) <- c("CHR", "SNP", "CM", "POS", "ALT", "REF")
ref_eur <- GWAS_QC(ref_eur, 0.01)
ref_afr <- GWAS_QC(ref_afr, 0.01)
annot <- fread("/scratch/negishi/chen4422/UKBB_pheSVD-main/ukb_geno/in_sample_ld/baselineLF_v2.2.UKB/annot_combine/first_three_columns.annot")

afr_file <- "/scratch/negishi/chen4422/hapnest/multi-ans-sum-stats/Lipids_all_of_us_v8/formatted/DBP_v8_GWAS_afr_regenie_results_From5_20250417_combined_format_noMHC.csv.gz"
eur_file <- "/scratch/negishi/chen4422/hapnest/multi-ans-sum-stats/Lipids_all_of_us_v8/formatted/DBP_v8_GWAS_eur_regenie_results_From5_20250417_combined_format_noMHC.csv.gz"

# QC each ancestry against its own reference, without cross-ancestry intersection.
afrdata_qced <- read_sumstats(afr_file, ref_afr)
eurdata_qced <- read_sumstats(eur_file, ref_eur)

eurdata_tofinemap <- eurdata_qced %>% filter(SNP %in% annot$SNP)
afrdata_tofinemap <- afrdata_qced %>% filter(SNP %in% annot$SNP)

# Write separate ancestry-specific summary statistics and reference lists.
trait <- "DBP"
out_dir <- file.path("aou_union_example", "summary_statistics")
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
for (anc in c("EUR", "AFR")) {
  ss <- as.data.frame(if (anc == "EUR") eurdata_tofinemap else afrdata_tofinemap)
  prefix <- file.path(out_dir, paste0(trait, "_", anc, "_GRCh38_combined_format_noMHC_to_finemap"))
  fwrite(ss, paste0(prefix, ".csv"))
  fwrite(ss[, c("SNP", "REF")], paste0(prefix, "_ref_flip"), col.names = FALSE, sep = " ")
  fwrite(ss[, "SNP", drop = FALSE], paste0(prefix, "_snplist"), col.names = FALSE)
}
```

ALT and REF alleles need to be consistent across ancestry groups. The All of Us summary statistics used here are already harmonized; for other sources see [this document](https://borangao.github.io/meSuSie_Analysis/GWAS_QC.html).

---

### 2. Align GWAS Summary Statistics with LD Reference Panel

**Goal:** Construct ancestry-matched LD reference genotypes from 1KG that **match each ancestry’s own** GWAS variant list and use the same REF/ALT orientation, avoiding sign errors in Z-scores.

We use `plink2` to subset 1KG genotypes (`--extract`), enforce REF allele orientation (`--ref-allele`), and output a new `.bed/.bim/.fam` file (`--make-bed`).

```{r step2, eval=FALSE}
trait <- "DBP"
kg_dir <- file.path("aou_union_example", "ld_reference")
dir.create(kg_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
align_ld_ref("EUR", trait, kg_base = kg_base, ss_dir = out_dir, out_base = kg_dir)
align_ld_ref("AFR", trait, kg_base = kg_base, ss_dir = out_dir, out_base = kg_dir)
```

---

### 3. LD Reference Construction

Below, we use the region spanning **58,658,279–59,673,534 bp on chromosome 20** (DBP) as an illustrative example. `build_ld_matrix()` extracts SNPs in the region, runs plink2, flags monomorphic variants, and writes the LD correlation matrix.

```{r step3, eval=FALSE}
trait   <- "DBP"
kg_dir <- file.path("aou_union_example", "ld_reference")
eur_ref <- fread(file.path(kg_dir, paste0("1kg_eur_maf_unrelated_biallelic_nodup_extracted_", trait, "_flipped.bim")))
afr_ref <- fread(file.path(kg_dir, paste0("1kg_afr_maf_unrelated_biallelic_nodup_extracted_", trait, "_flipped.bim")))

start <- 58658279; end <- 59673534

build_ld_matrix(eur_ref, chr_num = 20, start_pos = start, end_pos = end,
                bfile   = file.path(kg_dir, paste0("1kg_eur_maf_unrelated_biallelic_nodup_extracted_", trait, "_flipped")),
                out_dir = file.path("aou_union_example", paste0("risk_loci_ld_eur_", trait)))

build_ld_matrix(afr_ref, chr_num = 20, start_pos = start, end_pos = end,
                bfile   = file.path(kg_dir, paste0("1kg_afr_maf_unrelated_biallelic_nodup_extracted_", trait, "_flipped")),
                out_dir = file.path("aou_union_example", paste0("risk_loci_ld_afr_", trait)))
```

---

### 4. LD Mismatch Detection

A common issue in fine-mapping is mismatch between summary statistics and the LD reference panel. We use `kriging_rss` from `susieR` to iteratively identify and remove SNPs whose Z-scores are inconsistent with the LD structure. `filter_ld_mismatch()` handles the full loop automatically.

```{r step4, eval=FALSE}
trait <- "DBP"

geno_dir_eur <- file.path("aou_union_example", paste0("risk_loci_ld_eur_", trait))
geno_dir_afr <- file.path("aou_union_example", paste0("risk_loci_ld_afr_", trait))

afr_sumstats <- fread(file.path(out_dir, paste0(trait, "_AFR_GRCh38_combined_format_noMHC_to_finemap.csv")))
eur_sumstats <- fread(file.path(out_dir, paste0(trait, "_EUR_GRCh38_combined_format_noMHC_to_finemap.csv")))

afr_res <- filter_ld_mismatch(geno_dir_afr, "loci_example", afr_sumstats)
eur_res <- filter_ld_mismatch(geno_dir_eur, "loci_example", eur_sumstats)

data_dir <- file.path("aou_union_example", paste0("results_", trait), "summary_data")
dir.create(data_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
fwrite(afr_res$sumstats, file.path(data_dir, "afr_loci_example_summ"))
fwrite(eur_res$sumstats, file.path(data_dir, "eur_loci_example_summ"))
fwrite(afr_res$cov,      file.path(data_dir, "afr_loci_example.ld"), sep = " ")
fwrite(eur_res$cov,      file.path(data_dir, "eur_loci_example.ld"), sep = " ")
```


---

### 5. Variant Harmonization

Combine the post-QC summary statistics and LD from the preceding steps, retaining both common and ancestry-unique variants.

Match functional annotations to variants by rsID and allele pair, excluding missing or ambiguous matches. `DBP_chr20_annotations.rds` below is the resulting numeric annotation matrix, with SNP IDs as row names.

```{r save-observed-inputs, eval=FALSE}
to_infuse_summary <- function(ss) {
  ss <- as.data.frame(ss)
  rename <- c(BETA = "Beta", SE = "Se", ALT = "A1", REF = "A2")
  for (old in names(rename)) {
    if (old %in% names(ss)) names(ss)[names(ss) == old] <- rename[[old]]
  }
  if (!"Z" %in% names(ss)) ss$Z <- ss$Beta / ss$Se
  ss
}
summary_stat_list <- list(
  EUR = to_infuse_summary(eur_res$sumstats),
  AFR = to_infuse_summary(afr_res$sumstats)
)
R_mat_list <- list(EUR = eur_res$cov, AFR = afr_res$cov)
annot <- readRDS("data/DBP_chr20_annotations.rds")
stopifnot(!is.null(rownames(annot)))

ref <- do.call(rbind, summary_stat_list)
ref <- ref[!duplicated(ref$SNP), ]
ref <- ref[order(ref$CHR, ref$POS, ref$SNP), ]
union_ids <- ref$SNP[ref$SNP %in% rownames(annot)]
allele_ref <- ref[match(union_ids, ref$SNP), c("SNP", "A1", "A2")]
for (anc in names(summary_stat_list)) {
  ss <- summary_stat_list[[anc]]
  ss <- ss[ss$SNP %in% union_ids, ]
  summary_stat_list[[anc]] <- ss
  R_mat_list[[anc]] <- R_mat_list[[anc]][ss$SNP, ss$SNP, drop = FALSE]
}
observed <- list(
  summary_stat_list = summary_stat_list,
  R_mat_list = R_mat_list,
  annot = annot[union_ids, , drop = FALSE],
  union_ids = union_ids,
  allele_ref = allele_ref
)
dir.create("data", showWarnings = FALSE)
saveRDS(observed, "data/DBP_chr20_observed.rds")
```

```{r prepared-example-inputs, include=FALSE}
# Load the saved example when rendering this page independently.
observed <- readRDS(Sys.getenv(
  "INFUSE_AOU_EXAMPLE_INPUT", "data/DBP_chr20_observed.rds"
))
```

```{r prepare-union, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
prep <- prepare_infuse_union(
  summary_stat_list = observed$summary_stat_list,
  R_mat_list = observed$R_mat_list,
  annot = observed$annot,
  annot_ids = rownames(observed$annot),
  union_ids = observed$union_ids,
  allele_ref = observed$allele_ref,
  ld_allele_coding = "ancestry_effect",
  require_complete_ld_dimnames = TRUE
)

colSums(prep$variant_available)
table(prep$variant_map$availability_pattern)
```

After annotation matching, the example contains **2,890 variants**: 1,867 common variants and 1,023 ancestry-unique variants (241 EUR-only and 782 AFR-only). EUR and AFR contribute 2,108 and 2,649 variants, respectively.

The function `prepare_infuse_union()` aligns SNPs and harmonizes alleles across the ancestry-specific inputs, retaining both common and ancestry-unique variants. Set `ld_allele_coding = "ancestry_effect"` when LD follows each ancestry’s effect-allele coding, as in this example, or `"reference"` when LD already follows `allele_ref`. The returned `prep$variant_available` records the availability of common and ancestry-unique variants in each ancestry.

Continue to [Run INFUSE](Run_INFUSE.html) to fine-map this locus.
